title: Prescriptive Telemetry Handoff & Operational Roles for Enterprise Onboarding
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook defines a prescriptive, role-based telemetry handoff used during enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference. It focuses on what signals must be collected, minimal quality requirements for those signals, ownership of dashboards and alerts, and an operational escalation ladder that meshes Customer Success (CSM), Integration Engineering, and SRE responsibilities. Use this document as the canonical handoff checklist before signoff on the production acceptance gate.

Scope
- Applies to Dedicated and Private customers during the final 2 weeks of onboarding and first 30 days of production.
- Covers: request/response traces, per-tenant cost telemetry, model inference metrics, ingress/egress latency, error-classification, and synthetic health checks.
- Does not replace security/compliance artifacts (use the enterprise-deployment-compliance-evidence playbook for that).

Goals
1. Ensure telemetry provides sufficient context for rapid incident TTR (time-to-repair).
2. Prevent noisy alerts while surfacing customer-impacting anomalies.
3. Establish clear owner for each telemetry artifact to be handed to the customer operations contact.

Required Roles & Responsibilities
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): primary contact for business-level escalations, coordinates QBR artifacts.
- Integration Engineer (IE): owns onboarding of telemetry exporters, verifies schema conformance, and performs initial dashboard walk-through.
- SRE / Site Reliability: owns alert rules, runbooks, and escalation endpoints; responsible for uptime SLO enforcement.
- Customer Ops/Platform Engineer: recipient of the handoff; validates telemetry ingestion and runbook mapping on their side.

Ownership Matrix (text-table)
| Artifact | Primary Owner | Secondary Owner | Acceptance Criteria |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Ingress latency (p50/p95/p99) per-tenant | SRE | IE | p95 < 200ms for interactive tenants; dashboard populated for 30d of test traffic |
| Token cost by model & tenant (hourly) | Finance-ops (CS) | SRE | Hourly granularity, cost-tagging matches billing account |
| Model output quality (evals/feature-set) | IE | Customer Success | Prompt set coverage >= 80% of critical flows |
| Error classification (4xx vs 5xx vs model-misbehavior) | SRE | IE | Errors grouped and sampled with 1:100 sampling for traces |
| Synthetic journey (end-to-end) | IE | Customer Ops | Synthetic every 1m, depl. region coverage, alerts on 3 consecutive failures |

Telemetry Contract (required fields)
- Required metric labels: tenant_id, model_name, route, region, request_id, sampling_rate.
- Required trace context: trace_id, parent_span_id, request_id, backend_node.
- Metric retention for onboarding: 90 days at 1m granularity, 13 months at 1h for billing alignment.

Onboarding Handoff Checklist (step-by-step)
1. Integration Engineer deploys telemetry exporter and shares example payloads in JSON. Example payload snippet: 
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-123",
  "model_name": "gptx-14b-q4",
  "latency_ms": 134,
  "p99_estimate": 210,
  "request_id": "r-7d6c4",
  "region": "us-west-2"
}
```
2. SRE verifies metrics in Redwood internal metrics cluster and confirms retention policy.
3. IE and Customer Ops complete dashboard walk-through: top-tokens trend, cost burn, and failure heatmap.
4. Runbooks attached and smoke-tested (see "Runbook Tests" section).
5. Final signoff: CSM confirms business acceptance and schedules the first QBR cadence.

Alert Thresholds & SLO Mapping
- Production SLOs (enterprise tier): Availability 99.95% (per-tenant), P99 inference latency < 350ms for up to 64-token responses.
- Initial onboarding alert thresholds (conservative to reduce noise):
  - Synthetic journey failure: 3 failures in 5 minutes -> Pager to IE oncall.
  - P95 latency deviation > 2x baseline for 10m -> Pager to SRE.
  - Hourly cost anomaly > +60% vs rolling 7-day median -> Alert to CSM & Finance-ops.

Runbook Tests (acceptance scenarios)
- Test A: Simulate KV cache miss storm and verify KV cache miss-rate metric rises and a specific runbook step (scale read replicas) succeeds.
- Test B: Induce model swap (canary -> full) and validate fallback policy triggers and customer route fails over to compatibility model.
- Test C: Inject 5xx error rate and validate triage classification and alert routing (CSM notified, IE paged if persistent).

Escalation Ladder (operational flow)
1. Detect: Oncall receives alert, triages using dashboard + recent traces.
2. Contain: If customer-facing, enable temporary traffic shaping/fairshare and notify CSM.
3. Remediate: Execute runbook steps; if unknown, escalate to Engineering on-call with labeled artifact (trace + minimal repro).
4. Postmortem: If P1 outage or persistent regression, SRE owns RCA within 72 hours and CSM prepares customer-facing summary for QBR.

Integration Checklist for Customer (action items)
- Provide service account with read-only access to exported metrics and traces.
- Validate tenant_id mapping and confirm billing_account tag.
- Run synthetic suite provided by IE for 48h and report anomalies.
- Confirm on-call contact list and escalation phone numbers.

QBR & Ongoing Health Handover
- After 30 days of production, handoff artifacts for the QBR should include: cost delta by model, top 5 failure modes, synthetic pass rate, and any closed RCA actions.
- CSM schedules QBR and invites IE + SRE for the technical deep-dive.

Templates & Attachments (inlined)
- Dashboard template IDs: dashboard.enterprise-onboard.tokens (ID: db-4421), dashboard.enterprise-onboard.errors (ID: db-4422).
- Runbook snippet: "Scale GPU pool -> verify KV cache warmup -> validate p95 latency <= baseline".

Acceptance & Signoff
- Acceptance signoff requires: telemetry checks green (all required artifacts present), 48h synthetic stability, and runbook smoke tests passed. Signoff by IE, SRE, and CSM.

Related pages and references
- See also: enterprise-onboarding/post-provisioning-stability-checklist-2026 for provisioning steps; model-migration-cutover-governance-telemetry-sla-carveouts-2027 for model upgrade notes.

Notes & Rationale
- This playbook biases for explicit telemetry contracts to reduce time-to-diagnosis across organizational boundaries. We prefer short, testable acceptance criteria rather than vague assurances.
